chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad al-Nahdī, from Muḥammad ibn al-Walīd, from ʿUmar ibn Yazīd, who said:
I heard Abā ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام saying: Joining [the rounds] is only disliked in the obligatory [tawaf]; but as for the supererogatory, then no, by Allah, there is no harm in it.

key_terms.النَّافِلَةِ: the supererogatory or non-obligatory act of worship
key_terms.الْقِرَانُ: joining together multiple rounds in tawaf
key_terms.يُكْرَهُ: is considered disliked in legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Is joining multiple rounds in tawaf disliked in obligatory worship but allowed in supererogatory worship?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal distinction regarding qirān between rounds in tawaf: it is disliked in the obligatory form, but there is no problem with it in the supererogatory form. The narration therefore indicates a ruling differentiating between faridah and nafilah in acts of worship.
